original_value: This article presents the design and implementation of an event-triggered control approach, applied to the leader-following consensus and formation of a group of autonomous micro-aircraft with capabilities of vertical take-off and landing (VTOL-UAVs). The control strategy is based on an inner–outer loop control approach. The inner control law stabilizes the attitude and position of one agent, whereas the outer control follows a virtual leader to achieve position consensus cooperatively through an event-triggered policy. The communication topology uses undirected and connected graphs. With such an event-triggered control, the closed-loop trajectories converge to a compact sphere, centered in the origin of the error space. Furthermore, the minimal inter-sampling time is proven to be below bounded avoiding the Zeno behavior. The formation problem addresses the group of agents to fly in a given shape configuration. The simulation and experimental results highlight the performance of the proposed control strategy.

result.paraphrase: This article describes the design and implementation of an event-triggered control scheme for leader-following consensus and formation of a group of autonomous vertical take-off and landing micro-aircraft (VTOL-UAVs). The strategy uses an inner–outer loop control structure: the inner law stabilizes one agent’s attitude and position, while the outer loop tracks a virtual leader to achieve cooperative position consensus through an event-triggered policy. The communication topology is modeled by undirected, connected graphs. Under this control, the closed-loop trajectories converge to a compact sphere centered at the origin of the error space, and the minimum inter-sampling time is shown to be lower-bounded, preventing Zeno behavior. The formation task concerns making the agents fly in a prescribed shape configuration. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.
